title: Moving the games onto a 4 KB kernel
subtitle: Every game got bigger. Here is each byte, and what it bought.
lead: Four games now run on Fizlet's kernel, which has a 4 KB gzip budget. Battlefield Blitz ships on it; Null Invaders, Byte Runner and Sherman Bytes are in review. Every one got bigger in gzip bytes, by 7 to 21%. Most of the growth is the shared button kit. The rest buys steps that never allocate, runs that replay from a seed and one shell for three games.

body.text: A port keeps gameplay. Same numbers, same controller API, and the page comes back byte for byte. What changes is underneath: one engine per run, the rules as one system on typed arrays, and the bricks.

items: **Battlefield Blitz: shipped.** It ran on Fizlet first. Its port (0.8.0) made it replay from a seed and moved its supply crates onto `fizlet/rules`. It is on Fizlet 0.14.1 now.
**Null Invaders 1.0.0: in review.** The first game on `fizlet/arcade`; the shell was extracted from it.
**Byte Runner 1.0.0: in review.** The maze is SVG inside the page, through the arcade's `ctx.attach`.
**Sherman Bytes 1.0.0: in review.** Waves, airdrops and cannon tiers come from `fizlet/rules`.
**Swarm Protocol: in progress.** It moves onto the kernel and bricks and keeps its own shell and API. The four hooks it needs shipped in Fizlet 0.14.0.
**DOM Battlefield: next.** The plan keeps its model as the logic layer; only its score and supply code moves.

body.text: The three arcade ports wait on one design answer, not on code: their scoreboards now wear the Board UI kit, DOM Battlefield's keys and readouts.

blocks.heading: Before and after, in gzip bytes
blocks.subhead: From the size ledger: the shipped file when the game reports one, else the measured bundle. Nothing is estimated.

items.title: Battlefield Blitz: 31,011 → 33,254 B (+2,243 B, +7.2%)
items.body: Measured bundle. Moving to Fizlet 0.10.0 added 1,436 B; the crates on `fizlet/rules` brought it to 33,286 B, and reading crate age from the brick to 33,254 B. Blitz baked in the kit CSS before its port.

items.title: Null Invaders: 22,940 → 26,434 B (+3,494 B, +15.2%)
items.body: Without the kit CSS (2,702 B): 23,732 B, +792 B. The general arcade shell costs Null 321 B more than its own shell did.

items.title: Byte Runner: 29,160 → 33,868 B (+4,708 B, +16.1%)
items.body: Without the kit CSS (2,962 B): 30,906 B, +1,746 B. Its rules moved from objects to typed arrays: actors, a compiled maze graph, preallocated chase fields. Longer source, and a step that never allocates.

items.title: Sherman Bytes: 26,994 → 32,606 B (+5,612 B, +20.8%)
items.body: Without the kit CSS (3,060 B): 29,546 B, +2,552 B. Typed-array rules, and the step asks the page through `hitAt` and `nearAt`.

items.title: Swarm Protocol: 32,125 B today
items.body: The baseline. Its port moves the food checks out of the step and into the read phase. The plan expects the game chunk to grow, as every port's did; we will report it with and without what is shared.

body.text: The three arcade games grew 13,814 B together. 8,724 B of that is the kit CSS each one bakes in. Without it, they grew 79,094 → 84,184 B: +5,090 B, or 6.4%.
The kit buys one button language across the family. A key in Null Invaders presses like a key in DOM Battlefield. That is a shared look, not shared bytes.
`fizlet/arcade` is one shell for three games, but each game bundles its own copy. So the shell saves source and fixes, not bytes per game. It is general, too: action keys, any readouts, a meter.
Some layers did shrink, because that code is the engine's now. Byte Runner's clock went 925 → 252 B. Null's collision went 377 → 54 B, and its page code 386 → 100 B.

items: **Steps that never allocate.** Each arcade port has a test: 20,000 busy steps, 0 minor GCs.
**Runs that replay.** Each port has a same-seed test. Blitz played seed 41 twice over 3,600 frames, identical, with 0 `Math.random` calls in play.
**Gameplay held still.** Blitz 0.8.0 and 0.8.1 gave the same tanks, shells, bombs and crates for 5 seeds × 7,200 frames.
**Recall, tested.** Each arcade port's browser test checks that the page comes back byte for byte.
**A fix lands once.** In 0.12.1 the arcade scoreboard keys stopped breaking their labels over lines. One change in the shell fixed it for every game on it.

blocks.heading: What the ports taught the engine

body.text: **A number passed to a call V8 does not inline gets boxed.** That is one allocation each. A big game step stops V8 inlining, and Sherman's step boxed four numbers per shell per step.
That meant 5 minor GCs in 20,000 steps. Fizlet 0.13.0 added `hitAt(p, i)` and `nearAt(p, i, out)`: they read from a typed array, so nothing boxes. The count went to 0.

**`Math.hypot` allocates on every call in V8.** Byte Runner's ported step still made minor GCs, and a heap sample put almost all of them in `Math.hypot`. With `Math.sqrt(x * x + y * y)` instead, 20,000 busy steps make none.

**A getter that returns a number can box it.** The page brick read its refresh clock through `engine.time`: 12 B a frame, found with the sampling heap profiler. Since 0.15.0 it reads `engine.timing`, a typed array.

**Tests that wait on the wall clock flake.** The camera test waited 120 ms for a move and failed twice on CI. It now waits frame by frame. Blitz's friendly-fire test failed about 1 run in 10; with seed 7, a stopped clock and fixed steps, it passed 10 of 10.

**Test files run in parallel skew GC counts.** CPU contention delays V8's background compiler, so a check can run unoptimised. Under load, one check read 14 young GCs instead of 3. Run one file at a time, it passed 20 of 20.

**A zero-GC test only proves the paths it drives.** So the acceptance for a port also scans the step for `Math.random`, `Math.hypot` and wall-clock reads. It already found `Math.hypot` left in one draft's step, to fix before it ships.

items.q: Did any game get smaller on Fizlet?
items.a: No. All four grew, by 7.2% to 20.8% in gzip bytes. Without the kit CSS, the three arcade games grew 6.4% together.

items.q: Why share a shell if each game still bundles a copy?
items.a: Source and fixes. One shell means one place for a fix, one set of tests and one controller the hub drives. It does not mean fewer bytes per game.

items.q: How do you know the steps never allocate?
items.a: Each arcade port runs 20,000 busy steps after a warm-up and counts minor GCs with Node's GC observer, best of three windows. All three read 0.

items.q: When do Swarm Protocol and DOM Battlefield move?
items.a: Swarm Protocol is in progress; its engine hooks shipped in Fizlet 0.14.0. DOM Battlefield is next. Neither has a date.
